## Problem 1

Created function. It is in `source/birthday_repeated.R`

### Run this function 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50.
```{r}

source("source/birthday_repeated.R")

birthday_results_df =
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )

birthday_results_df

```

### For each group size, compute the probability that at least two people in the group will share a birthday by averaging across the 10000 simulation runs
```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) 

```

### Plot showing the probability as a function of group size
```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```

This plot shows that the greater the group size, the higher the probability that two people in the group will share a birthday. There only needs to be about 23 people in the group for there to be a 50% chance that two people in the group will share a birthday.


## Problem 2

```{r}
study_df = 
  tibble(
files = list.files("data/data"))
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

source("source/file_import.R")

study_df = study_df |> 
  mutate(
    file_df = map(files, file_import)
    ) |> 
  unnest(file_df) |> 
    separate(col = files, into = c("arm", "study_id"), sep = "_") |> 
  mutate(
    arm = case_match(
      arm,
      "con" ~ "control",
      "exp" ~ "experimental"
    ),
    study_id = str_remove(study_id, "\\.csv")
  )

study_df

```

```{r}
study_df |> 
ggplot(aes(x = week, y = value, group = study_id, color = study_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(~arm)
```

Those in the control arm have lower values on average compared to those in the experimental arm. While the values of those in the experimental arm tend to increase as the weeks go on, the values of those in the control arm tend to stay the same or decrease. 

## Problem 3
```{r cache=TRUE}

source("source/sim_t_test.R")

sim_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    true_mu = 0:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    est_df = map(true_mu, sim_t_test)
  ) |> 
  unnest(est_df) |> 
  mutate(
    rejected = p_value < 0.05
  )
```

```{r}
sim_results_df |> 
  group_by(true_mu) |> 
  summarize(power = mean(rejected)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = power)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Statistical Power vs. True Effect Size",
    x = "True Mean",
    y = "Power (Proportion Rejected)"
  )
```

As the value of the true mean increases, the power increases. 100% power is achieved with a true mean of about 5.


```{r}
sim_results_df |> 
  group_by(true_mu) |> 
  summarize(
    all_samples = mean(mu_hat),
    rejected_samples = mean(mu_hat[rejected])
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    c(all_samples, rejected_samples),
    names_to = "sample_group",
    values_to = "avg_mu_hat"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = avg_mu_hat, color = sample_group)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_discrete(
    labels = c("All Samples", "Null Rejected")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Estimated Mean vs. True Mean",
    x = "True Mean",
    y = "Average Estimate",
    color = "Subset"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



```
 
 The sample average of 𝜇̂ across tests for which the null is rejected is NOT approximately equal to the true value of 𝜇. We can see in the plot that the average of 𝜇̂ across tests for which the null is rejected is higher than the true value of 𝜇 when the true mean is equal to anywhere between a little over 0 and 4.
